title: Egidiuslied
author: Anonymous (Gruuthuse manuscript)
context: Carton's 1849 edition prints this Middle Dutch lyric as number XCVIII in 19 lines. Its middle refrain reads 'de doot'; the first and last have 'die doot'. The manuscript abbreviates the final refrain; Carton expands three lines, while some editions expand five, for 21 lines. These are readings of one work, not separate poems. Authorship is disputed. KANTL identifies it individually as the manuscript's best-known song; this is not a global ranking. Belgium is an associated modern place.
rights: This historical poem reading is public domain in the United States. The 1849 printing predates 1909; editor Charles Carton died in 1863. Copyright, edition-related and moral rights vary by jurisdiction; check local law. The scan is linked, not republished; no translation, score or recording is included.
text:
Egidius, waer bestu bleven?
Mi lanct na di, gheselle mijn;
Du coors die doot, du liets mi tleven.
Dat was gheselscap goet ende fijn,
Het sceen teen moeste ghestorven sijn.

Nu bestu in den troon verheven
Claerre dan der zonnen scijn;
Alle vruecht es di ghegheven.

Egidius, waer bestu bleven?
Mi lanct na di, gheselle mijn,
Du coors de doot, du liets mi tleven.

Nu bidt vor mi, ic moet noch sneven,
Ende in de weerelt liden pijn;
Verware mijn stede di beneven,
Ic moet noch zinghen een liedekijn;
Nochtan moet emmer ghestorven sijn.

Egidius, waer bestu bleven?
Mi lanct na di, gheselle mijn;
Du coors die doot, du liets mi tleven.

title: Kinder-lijck
author: Joost van den Vondel
sourceTitle: Van Lennep · De werken van Vondel · 1857 · p. 157
context: The 1857 Van Lennep edition prints this separately headed elegy in 16 lines. Its opening reads 'Konstantijntje'; the 1644-based critical edition reads 'Constantijntje' and differs in other spellings. The poem is commonly dated 1632, though 1633 is also suggested. The printed alternating indentation is retained; long s and punctuation typography are normalized. A Dutch teachers' survey selection names this individual poem, not a global ranking. The Netherlands is an associated place.
rights: This historical poem reading is public domain in the United States. Vondel died in 1679 and 1857 editor Jacob van Lennep in 1868. Copyright, edition-related and moral rights vary by jurisdiction; check local law. The scan is linked, not republished; no translation, score or recording is included.
text:
Konstantijntje, ’t saligh kijntje,
  Cherubijntje, van om hoogh,
d’Ydelheden, hier beneden,
  Uytlacht met een lodderoogh.
Moeder, seyt hy, waerom schreyt ghy?
  Waerom greyt ghy, op mijn lijck?
Boven leef ick, boven sweef ick,
  Engeltje van ’t hemelrijck:
En ick blinck’ er, en ick drinck’ er,
  ’t Geen de schincker alles goeds
Schenckt de sielen, die daer krielen,
  Dertel van veel overvloeds.
Leer dan reysen, met gepeysen,
  Na palleysen, uyt het slick
Deser werrelt, die soo dwerrelt.
  Eeuwigh gaet voor oogenblick.

title: Amor constante más allá de la muerte
author: Francisco de Quevedo
sourceTitle: El Parnasso español · 1650 · p. 190 · Boston Public Library
searchAliases: Cerrar podrá mis ojos la postrera
context: The 1650 printing separately heads this complete 14-line sonnet. Its fifth line has an extra 'se' in 'Mas no se de essotra parte'; the 1648 edition lacks it. The 1650 reading also has plural 'dejaràn' and 'ceniça'; some modern editions emend the verb to singular. Long s, indentation and punctuation typography are normalized, without combining editions. UNAM's description cites Dámaso Alonso on the sonnet's reception, not a global ranking. Spain is an associated place.
rights: This historical poem reading is public domain in the United States. Quevedo died in 1645 and editor González de Salas in 1651. Copyright, edition-related and moral rights vary by jurisdiction; check local law. The scan is linked, not republished; no translation, score or recording is included.
text:
Cerrar podrà mis ojos la postrera
Sombra, que me llevare el blanco dia;
I podrà desatar esta alma mia
Hora, a su afan ansioso lisonjera:
Mas no se de essotra parte en la rivera
Dejarà la memoria, en donde ardia;
Nadar sabe mi llama la agua fria,
I perder el respeto a lei severa.
Alma, a quien todo un Dios prission ha sido,
Venas, que humor a tanto fuego han dado,
Medulas, que han gloriosamente ardido,
Su cuerpo dejaràn, no su cuidado
Seran ceniça, mas tendrà sentido;
Polvo seràn, mas polvo enamorado.
